description: ¡Hola! Somos Misti Sound, un equipo de Arequipa compitiendo en el reto "The Earth Information Jukebox". Nuestro proyecto se enfoca en la sonificación de datos científicos reales, transformando la información geológica y climática de la Tierra en experiencias sonoras y musicales. Llevar el nombre de nuestro gran volcán es nuestra firma para representar con orgullo nuestra identidad arequipeña.
summary:
Misti Sound is an interactive "Terrestrial Jukebox" that transforms real NASA data into a comparative sound experience: it allows you to hear what the sky in your city sounded like the month you were born and how it sounds today, complemented by a voice narration detailing the environmental data behind the change and a Teacher's Guide for education.

The application addresses the challenge of accessibility and scientific understanding by breaking the exclusively visual dependence of Earth observation. By translating complex climate variables into clear sound contrasts and narrated explanations, it makes environmental evidence intuitive, emotional, and easy to share on social media.

This project is important because it democratizes access to science for visually impaired individuals, students, teachers, and citizens in general. By turning abstract data into a personal story on equal terms, it transforms every user into an informed and active environmental advocate.
details:
1. What does it do or how does it work?

Misti Sound is an interactive Earth Information Jukebox that transforms NASA environmental data into music, narration, and 3D visualizations. Users enter their city and date of birth to explore how the planet has changed throughout their lifetime.

The platform presents three interactive 3D globes displaying CO₂ emissions (NASA SVS), ozone levels (NASA Aura OMI), and temperature anomalies (NASA GISTEMP v4).

Through a personalized narrator, users travel across three periods: the 1950s, their birth year, and recent years. Each environmental variable is converted into sound using original algorithms:

  • CO₂: Higher concentrations generate more frequent sonic flashes.
  • Ozone: Lower ozone levels produce stronger, brighter wind sounds.
  • Temperature: Rising temperatures transform calm piano melodies into increasingly intense compositions.

Finally, users can share their experiences and leave messages for future generations, encouraging reflection and environmental awareness.

2. What benefits does it have?

Misti Sound makes complex scientific information easier to understand through interactive storytelling, sound, and visualization.

Its main benefit is accessibility: people with visual impairments can experience environmental data through audio narration and sonification rather than relying exclusively on visual representations.

The platform also supports environmental education, encourages emotional connections with climate information, and allows users to share their discoveries through social media.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

Our main objective is to transform young people from passive observers of climate change into active environmental advocates.

By connecting scientific data with personal experiences, Misti Sound seeks to inspire environmental awareness, responsible decisions, and community participation.

We also aim to promote inclusive environmental education, ensuring that people with visual impairments have greater opportunities to explore and understand scientific information.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

Misti Sound was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with Vite supporting the development process.

We used CesiumJS and Three.js for interactive 3D visualizations, Tone.js for algorithmic music generation, and NASA datasets, including SVS, Aura OMI, and GISTEMP v4, for environmental information.

Python was used for data preparation, GitHub for version control and team collaboration, and Netlify for web deployment configuration.

We also used ChatGPT Codex, Claude Code, and Gemini as AI-assisted development tools to support programming, debugging, and improvements.

The platform operates through a web browser and does not require specialized hardware.

5. How is your project creative?

Misti Sound introduces an innovative approach to environmental education by turning scientific measurements into an emotional and musical experience.

Instead of presenting climate change exclusively through graphs and statistics, the project allows users to hear environmental changes through original algorithmic compositions.

Its creativity lies in combining personalized storytelling, interactive 3D globes, accessible audio, and environmental science.

The music is generated through algorithms based on actual environmental values, rather than by generative AI, making every sound directly connected to the data.

6. What factors did your team consider?

Our team focused on six essential factors: scientific accuracy, accessibility, educational impact, user experience, technical feasibility, and environmental awareness.

We prioritized reliable NASA datasets and transparency. Historical estimates and projections are identified with the symbol "≈" and explained to users to avoid presenting approximations as direct measurements.

Accessibility was also a priority, including narration, adaptable interfaces, and keyboard controls.

Finally, our team integrated expertise in user experience, web development, geospatial visualization, audio engineering, and NASA data analysis to create a meaningful, inclusive, and engaging educational experience.
